claim.pdf_says: Index entries printed one per line with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry, e.g. 'Configuration Section, IV-31' followed by the indented sub-entry 'Nucleus, VI-9'
claim.markdown_says: Every entry is a bare line with no list marker, sub-entries only space-indented: 'Configuration Section, IV-31' then '  Nucleus, VI-9'
claim.why_it_matters: Markdown renders consecutive bare lines as one paragraph, so the whole index page collapses into one run-on line and the entry boundaries and main-entry/sub-entry hierarchy are lost when rendered (pages 961-962 use nested '- ' list items and keep them). Index is informative; the entry text and page references themselves match the PDF.

verdict.reasoning: Checked the 300 dpi render of PDF page 964 (B-52, Index, two columns Conditional sentence .. Definitions) against page-964.md. Every main entry, every sub-entry and every page reference is present in order, each on its own source line, and the sub-entries keep their indentation (two spaces; wrapped continuations four), so the PDF's entry boundaries and hierarchy are carried in the transcription text. The only difference is markup style: no '- ' list markers, unlike pages 961-962 (page 963 uses the same bare-line style). That is a rendering/formatting difference of an informative index, not a content discrepancy; the claim itself concedes the text and references match. Rejected as formatting only.
